Pakistan :: part 04 :: chunk_0003
**Pakistan**,[[f]](#cite_note-13) officially the **Islamic Republic of Pakistan**,[[g]](#cite_note-14) is a country in [South Asia](/wiki/South_Asia "South Asia"). It is the [fifth-most populous country](/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_population "List of countries and dependencies by population"), with a population of over 241.5 million,[[d]](#cite_note-fn3-10) having the [second-largest Muslim population](/wiki/Islam_by_country#Countries "Islam by country") as of 2023. [Islamabad](/wiki/Islamabad "Islamabad") is the nation's capital, while [Karachi](/wiki/Karachi "Karachi") is [its largest city](/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Pakistan_by_population "List of cities in Pakistan by population") and [financial centre](/wiki/Financial_centre "Financial centre"). Pakistan is the [33rd-largest country by area](/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_area "List of countries and dependencies by area"). Bounded by the [Arabian Sea](/wiki/Arabian_Sea "Arabian Sea") on the south, the [Gulf of Oman](/wiki/Gulf_of_Oman "Gulf of Oman") on the southwest, and the [Sir Creek](/wiki/Sir_Creek "Sir Creek") on the southeast, it shares land borders with [India](/wiki/India "India") to the east; [Afghanistan](/wiki/Afghanistan "Afghanistan") to the west; [Iran](/wiki/Iran "Iran") to the southwest; and [China](/wiki/China "China") to the northeast. It shares a maritime border with [Oman](/wiki/Oman "Oman") in the Gulf of Oman, and is separated from [Tajikistan](/wiki/Tajikistan "Tajikistan") in the northwest by Afghanistan's narrow [Wakhan Corridor](/wiki/Wakhan_Corridor "Wakhan Corridor").

Pakistan is the site of [several ancient cultures](/wiki/History_of_Pakistan "History of Pakistan"), including the 8,500-year-old [Neolithic](/wiki/Neolithic "Neolithic") site of [Mehrgarh](/wiki/Mehrgarh "Mehrgarh") in [Balochistan](/wiki/Balochistan,_Pakistan "Balochistan, Pakistan"), the [Indus Valley Civilisation](/wiki/Indus_Valley_Civilisation "Indus Valley Civilisation") of the [Bronze Age](/wiki/Bronze_Age "Bronze Age"),[[8]](#cite_note-Wright-2009-15) and the ancient [Gandhara civilisation](/wiki/Gandhara_civilisation "Gandhara civilisation").[[

At the time of team's inception, Rakuten created a pair of unnamed male and female golden eagle mascots.[[115]](#cite_note-clutch-116) The name Clutch (and the feminine Clutchena) was selected from approximately 6,500 suggestions that were solicited from the public. The name has a double meaning derived from the word "clutch", such as the grasp of an eagle's claw, as well as the baseball concept of a [clutch hitter](/wiki/Clutch_hitter "Clutch hitter").[[116]](#cite_note-mascot_names-117) Clutch wears a jersey bearing the number 10, an Eagles retired number that represents the fans. A third mascot, a [harpy eagle](/wiki/Harpy_eagle "Harpy eagle") named Switch, was unveiled in 2016.[[117]](#cite_note-118) The Eagles have also periodically featured an unofficial, mischievous mascot named Mr. Carrasco. The character, based on a black crow, is masked and rides a motorcycle.[[118]](#cite_note-119) For Black Eagles Day in 2017, Rakuten added a mascot character called Kurowashi-san. Unlike the other costumed mascots, Kurowashi-san appeared as a normal man with a black eagle on his head.[[119]](#cite_note-120)

The Golden Eagles farm team plays in the [Eastern League](/wiki/Eastern_League_(Japanese_baseball) "Eastern League (Japanese baseball)"). The team was founded in 2005.

The State of New York has a primarily urban population. The largest city in the state is [New York City](/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"), which is also one of the world's most ethnically diverse and cosmopolitan cities. Additional major urban centers include [Albany](/wiki/Albany,_New_York "Albany, New York"), [Buffalo](/wiki/Buffalo,_New_York "Buffalo, New York"), [Rochester](/wiki/Rochester,_New_York "Rochester, New York"), [Syracuse](/wiki/Syracuse,_New_York "Syracuse, New York") and [Utica](/wiki/Utica,_New_York "Utica, New York"). The state has 62 counties; the most populated one is [Kings County](/wiki/Kings_County,_New_York "Kings County, New York") ([Brooklyn](/wiki/Brooklyn,_New_York "Brooklyn, New York")). Much of New York State's population outside of New York City is concentrated in the [Long Island](/wiki/Long_Island "Long Island"), [Hudson Valley](/wiki/Hudson_Valley "Hudson Valley"), [Western New York](/wiki/Western_New_York "Western New York"), [Finger Lakes](/wiki/Finger_Lakes "Finger Lakes"), and [Capital District](/wiki/Capital_District_(New_York) "Capital District (New York)") regions; if the population of New York City is included, this amounts to 90% of the state's total population.

The intense development, urbanization and suburban sprawl of New York City makes it the most populated region in New York and the collective U.S., an estimated 20 to 30 million in the eight-state [Megalopolis](/wiki/Megalopolis_(city_type) "Megalopolis (city type)") stretching 500 miles from [Boston](/wiki/Boston "Boston") to [Washington, D.C.](/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C."), with New York City in the middle has 15 million residents in a 100-mile radius including [Philadelphia](/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia") (1.5 million in its city limits), northern [New Jersey](/wiki/New_Jersey "New Jersey") and [Connecticut](/wiki/Connecticut "Connecticut"). A simple majority of New York's population lives within two hours of New York City. Patterson was traded by the Cubs to the Orioles on January 9, 2006, for minor league players [Nate Spears](/wiki/Nate_Spears "Nate Spears") and Carlos Perez.[[1]](#cite_note-:0-1) On February 10, 2007, Patterson signed a 1-year deal worth $4.3 million to avoid arbitration.[[11]](#cite_note-11) In his first of two years with the [Orioles](/wiki/2006_Baltimore_Orioles_season "2006 Baltimore Orioles season"), he batted .276 with 16 home runs and 53 RBI. He also stole 45 bases, which ranked third in the [American League](/wiki/American_League "American League"). Patterson's contract was not renewed after the 2007 season.

Hou Yu-ih :: Early life and education :: chunk_0001
Hou was born on 7 June 1957, in [Puzi](/wiki/Puzi "Puzi"), [Chiayi County](/wiki/Chiayi_County "Chiayi County"), where his family owned a pork stall. As a child, Hou aided the family business by catching and butchering wild pigs.[[2]](#cite_note-indepth2024-5) He later recalled this his mother, Lyu Hsiu-lan, came from "simple and honest family" and "invested all her energy into her children."[[3]](#cite_note-:0-6) His father was a Taiwanese *[benshengren](/wiki/Benshengren "Benshengren")* who was conscripted to work as an aircraft mechanic in Japan during [World War II](/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") and then served in the [Republic of China Navy](/wiki/Republic_of_China_Navy "Republic of China Navy") alongside [Lee Teng-hui](/wiki/Lee_Teng-hui "Lee Teng-hui"). The senior Hou then fought in the [Chinese Civil War](/wiki/Chinese_Civil_War "Chinese Civil War") for the [Kuomintang](/wiki/Kuomintang "Kuomintang") before returning to Taiwan from [Shanghai](/wiki/Shanghai "Shanghai").[[4]](#cite_note-7)

After graduating from National Chiayi Senior High School, Hou decided to pursue a career in law enforcement as a member of the Taiwanese police force.[[3]](#cite_note-:0-6) He graduated from [Central Police University](/wiki/Central_Police_University "Central Police University") in 1980 with a [Bachelor of Arts](/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts") (B.A.) in [criminology](/wiki/Criminology "Criminology") and earned a [Ph.D.](/wiki/Ph.D. "Ph.D.") in crime prevention from the university in 2004.[[5]](#cite_note-8)[[6]](#cite_note-9) His doctoral dissertation was titled, "A study on sexual assault and homicide crimes in Taiwan" (Chinese: 台灣地區性侵害殺人犯罪之研究).[[7]](#cite_note-10) It examined 42 sexual assault and murder cases in Taiwan from 1995 to 2004, and was completed under Tsai Dehui, the president of the university, and Huang Fuyuan, the dean of academic affairs.[[8]](#cite_note-11)

Main article: [Supreme Court of the United States](/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States "Supreme Court of the United States")

The Supreme Court was created by [Article III](/wiki/Article_Three_of_the_United_States_Constitution "Article Three of the United States Constitution") of the [United States Constitution](/wiki/Constitution_of_the_United_States "Constitution of the United States"), which stipulates that the "judicial power of the United States, shall be vested in one Supreme Court,"[[4]](#cite_note-4) and was organized by the [1st United States Congress](/wiki/1st_United_States_Congress "1st United States Congress"). Through the [Judiciary Act of 1789](/wiki/Judiciary_Act_of_1789 "Judiciary Act of 1789"), Congress specified the Court's [original](/wiki/Original_jurisdiction "Original jurisdiction") and [appellate jurisdiction](/wiki/Appellate_jurisdiction "Appellate jurisdiction"), created thirteen judicial districts, and fixed the number of justices at six (one chief justice and five associate justices).[[5]](#cite_note-5)[[6]](#cite_note-6)

Since 1789, Congress has occasionally altered the size of the Supreme Court, historically in response to the country's own expansion in size. An [1801 act](/wiki/Midnight_Judges_Act "Midnight Judges Act") would have decreased the Court's size to five members upon its next vacancy. However, an [1802 act](/wiki/Judiciary_Act_of_1802 "Judiciary Act of 1802") negated the effects of the 1801 act upon the Court before any such vacancy occurred, maintaining the Court's size at six members. Later legislation increased its size to [seven members in 1807](/wiki/Seventh_Circuit_Act_of_1807 "Seventh Circuit Act of 1807"), to [nine in 1837](/wiki/Eighth_and_Ninth_Circuits_Act_of_1837 "Eighth and Ninth Circuits Act of 1837"), and to [ten in 1863](/wiki/Tenth_Circuit_Act_of_1863 "Tenth Circuit Act of 1863"). Hong Kong has a [humid subtropical climate](/wiki/Humid_subtropical_climate "Humid subtropical climate") ([Köppen](/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification") *Cwa*), characteristic of southern China, closely bordering on a [tropical monsoon climate](/wiki/Tropical_monsoon_climate "Tropical monsoon climate"). Summers are long, hot, and humid, with occasional showers and thunderstorms and warm air from the southwest. The humid climate of Hong Kong intensifies summer heat. [Typhoons](/wiki/Typhoon "Typhoon") occur most often then, sometimes resulting in floods or landslides. Also rarely occurring are [waterspouts](/wiki/Waterspout "Waterspout") and [tornadoes](/wiki/Tornado "Tornado"), which occurred at Hong Kong International Airport on 26 September 2020 and at Victoria Harbour on 28 September 2024.[[171]](#cite_note-177)[[172]](#cite_note-178) Winters are short, mild and usually sunny at the beginning, becoming cloudy towards February. Frequent cold fronts bring strong, cooling winds from the north and occasionally result in chilly weather. Autumn is the sunniest season, whilst spring is generally cloudy.[[173]](#cite_note-HKClimate-179) Snowfall has been extremely rare in Hong Kong; the last reported instance was on [Tai Mo Shan](/wiki/Tai_Mo_Shan "Tai Mo Shan") in 1975.[[174]](#cite_note-180) Hong Kong averages 1,709 hours of sunshine per year.[[175]](#cite_note-181) Historic temperature extremes at the [Hong Kong Observatory](/wiki/Hong_Kong_Observatory "Hong Kong Observatory") are 36.6 °C (97.9 °F) on 22 August 2017 and 0.0 °C (32.0 °F) on 18 January 1893, record highest daily minimum temperature there was 30.1 °C (86.2 °F) on 18 August 1990 and the lowest daily maximum temperature there was 3.2 °C (37.8 °F) on 16 January 1893.[[176]](#cite_note-182)[[177]](#cite_note-183)[[178]](#cite_note-184) The highest and lowest recorded temperatures in all of Hong Kong are 39.0 °C (102 °F) at [Wetland Park](/wiki/Hong_Kong_Wetland_Park "Hong Kong Wetland Park") on 22 August 2017,[[179]](#cite_note-185) and −6.0 °C (21.2 °F) at Tai Mo Shan [on 24 January 2016](/wiki/January_2016_Ea

Unlike other Indo-European languages, English has largely abandoned the inflectional [case system](/wiki/Case_system "Case system") in favour of [analytic](/wiki/Analytic_language "Analytic language") constructions. Only the [personal pronouns](/wiki/Personal_pronoun "Personal pronoun") retain morphological case more strongly than any other [word class](/wiki/Word_class "Word class"). English distinguishes at least seven major word classes: verbs, nouns, adjectives, adverbs, determiners (including articles), prepositions, and conjunctions. Some analyses add pronouns as a class separate from nouns, and subdivide conjunctions into [subordinators](/wiki/English_subordinators "English subordinators") and [coordinators](/wiki/English_coordinators "English coordinators"), and add the class of interjections.[[179]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHuddlestonPullum200222-179) English also has a rich set of [auxiliary verbs](/wiki/Auxiliary_verb "Auxiliary verb"), such as *have* and *do*, expressing the categories of mood and aspect. He was traded at the end of the season to the [New Orleans Pelicans](/wiki/New_Orleans_Pelicans "New Orleans Pelicans") in a trade package for [Anthony Davis](/wiki/Anthony_Davis "Anthony Davis"). He played two seasons with the Pelicans before joining the [Chicago Bulls](/wiki/Chicago_Bulls "Chicago Bulls") in a [sign-and-trade deal](/wiki/Sign-and-trade_deal "Sign-and-trade deal"), but a persistent knee injury sidelined him for the majority of his tenure with the team, with him missing the entirety of the [2022–23](/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Chicago_Bulls_season "2022–23 Chicago Bulls season") and [2023–24 seasons](/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_Chicago_Bulls_season "2023–24 Chicago Bulls season"). After the [2024–25](/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_Chicago_Bulls_season "2024–25 Chicago Bulls season") season, Ball was traded to the [Cleveland Cavaliers](/wiki/Cleveland_Cavaliers "Cleveland Cavaliers").
